pollers.note: The distributed poller fleet. Each pool's nodes are polled by the pollers registered to it; a pool with no live poller goes unmonitored.
pollers.unavailable: Poller management is unavailable in skeleton mode.

empty.title: No pollers yet
empty.sub: Pollers appear here once they connect to the bus and send a heartbeat. Use Register poller for the remote-site setup snippet.

gaps.title: Recent monitoring gaps
gaps.note: Windows when core lost contact with a poller. A poller that stayed up but was cut off backfills its metrics for the window on reconnect; alerts are not backfilled (they resume from now).

nodes.title: Nodes polled by {{id}}
nodes.note: The working set core has published to this poller — what stops being monitored if it goes away.
nodes.empty: This poller holds no nodes right now.
nodes.offline: This poller is offline, so it holds no working set.
nodes.unknown: This core is a standby, so it does not track poller assignments.

remove.title: Remove poller
remove.confirmText: Remove poller {{id}} from the inventory? If it reconnects it will re-register automatically.

register.title: Register a poller
register.intro: Run a poller container at the remote site; it connects outbound to the central NATS bus. Fill in its identity below, then drop the generated <env>.env</env> next to <file>docker-compose.poller.yml</file> and bring it up.
register.invalidToken: Use letters, digits, dash or underscore only.
register.snippetEmpty: Enter a valid ID, pool and bus URL to generate the snippet.

pool.label: Pool
pool.hint: Nodes assigned to this pool are polled here.

busUrl.label: Bus URL
busUrl.hint: Include the poller credentials; a TLS URL is required off-site.

caFile.label: CA file path (optional)
caFile.hint: Only when the bus cert is signed by a private CA.

health.note: Yagra's own health: the poll loop, its backing services, fleet data coverage, and host resources.

settings.note: System-wide monitoring defaults. Per-profile overrides take precedence over these.
settings.signInHint: Sign in with a config-management role to change this.

polling.title: Polling
polling.intervalHelp: How often each node is polled, unless its Device profile sets its own interval. {{min}}–{{max}} seconds.

err.range: Enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.

integrations.note: Connect external systems monitored through a vendor cloud API.
integrations.unavailable: Integrations are unavailable in skeleton mode (no store).

meraki.desc: Read-only Dashboard API monitoring — availability, uplinks, and traffic across your Meraki organizations.

more.name: More integrations
more.desc: Additional vendor and notification integrations will appear here in a future release.

polling.title: Meraki polling
polling.hint: Global safeguard — instantly halt all Meraki Dashboard API polling fleet-wide, without deleting any organization config.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.empty: No Meraki organizations yet. Add one to start monitoring.

addOrg.title: Add Meraki organization
addOrg.apiKeyHint: Use a read-only Dashboard API key. It is sealed (encrypted at rest) and never shown again. Yagra only ever issues read-only GET calls to Meraki.
addOrg.selectHint: Select the organizations to monitor. All share this one API key.
addOrg.noOrgs: This key can't access any organizations.

networks.title: Network scope — {{name}}
networks.hint: Only monitored networks are collected. Un-checking a network stops narrowing API calls to it (existing device nodes are untouched — remove them to stop monitoring a device).
networks.empty: No networks yet — run “Import devices” to enumerate the org first.

cadence.title: Cadence — {{name}}
cadence.rateBudgetHint: Conservative — kept well under the org API cap so the customer keeps headroom.

delete.title: Delete organization
delete.confirmText: Delete {{name}}? Its imported device nodes, network scope, and HostTree groups are removed. Metric history in the TSDB is left. This cannot be undone.

import.title: Import devices — {{name}}
import.allImported: No new devices to import — every device this key can see is already monitored.

err.discover: failed to reach the Meraki API
